news.headline: Michigan Democratic Senate candidates El‑Sayed and Stevens plan joint appearance amid feud
news.summary: Incumbent Rep. Haley Stevens and Senate candidate Abdul El‑Sayed will appear together in Detroit days before the midterm election. Their joint rally follows a dispute over an ad that Stevens says is anti‑Israel and a demand that El‑Sayed apologize for his comments. The two former primary rivals are trying to present party unity while their conflict draws attention from other Democrats. The outcome could affect the party’s chances in a key swing‑state Senate race.

news.headline: Federal judge dismisses charges against two former FBI officials in Hunter Biden laptop case
news.summary: U.S. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui dismissed a criminal complaint against former FBI agents Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, who were accused of lying to Congress about the Hunter Biden laptop investigation. The judge found no probable cause and criticized the prosecution as a rushed, politically motivated effort. The case stemmed from a Justice Department attempt to hold the agents accountable for alleged false statements. The dismissal removes a legal battle tied to the broader partisan debate over the laptop probe.

news.headline: Trump to deliver final midterm address at Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool
news.summary: President Donald Trump scheduled a speech at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool on Monday, the day before the midterm elections. The event will serve as his closing campaign message and will highlight initiatives his administration has pursued in Washington, D.C. The speech comes as both parties assess the potential impact on congressional control. The venue has recently been reopened after renovation work.

news.headline: DOJ seeks Supreme Court order to set aside 20,000 California mail ballots
news.summary: The Justice Department filed an emergency request with the Supreme Court asking it to require California to separate more than 20,000 mail-in ballots it says belong to likely non‑citizens. Federal judges have already rejected the administration’s bid, and the appeal comes one day before the November 3 election. The case centers on the department’s authority to intervene in state voter rolls and the credibility of the list of targeted voters. The outcome could affect ballot counting in a key swing state.

news.headline: Nine killed in Florida Learjet crash near West Palm Beach
news.summary: A Learjet 60 traveling from Austin, Texas to the Bahamas crashed in a residential area near Cresthaven, Florida, killing all nine people on board. U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy confirmed the fatalities and said the National Transportation Safety Board has opened an investigation. The crash occurred around 12:50 p.m. ET and was witnessed as a fireball that narrowly missed nearby homes. Authorities have not yet released a cause for the accident.

news.headline: Martha Stewart apologizes after backlash to homeless-themed Halloween costume
news.summary: The 85‑year‑old lifestyle icon posted an Instagram photo of herself dressed as a homeless person for Halloween, then deleted it and issued an apology. Critics said the costume was insensitive to people experiencing homelessness. Stewart said the intent was to raise awareness, but the incident sparked a broader debate about privilege and representation. The controversy highlights how public figures’ portrayals of marginalized groups can trigger intense public reaction.

news.headline: Federal judge dismisses DOJ lawsuit seeking to block Alaska Senate certification
news.summary: U.S. District Judge Sharon Gleason, an Obama appointee, dismissed a lawsuit filed by the Justice Department that aimed to delay certification of Alaska's U.S. Senate race if incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan lost. The suit argued that a candidate with a similar name could confuse voters and affect the outcome. The court found the administration had not shown how to remedy the alleged confusion. The decision leaves the election results to be certified without further judicial intervention.

news.headline: Rep. Haley Stevens defends last‑minute endorsement of GOP Senate candidate on CNN
news.summary: Rep. Haley Stevens (D‑MI) appeared on CNN's Anderson Cooper 360 to explain her decision to endorse Republican Mike Rogers over Democratic nominee Abdul El‑Sayed in the Michigan U.S. Senate race. She said the endorsement was based on concerns about El‑Sayed's behavior and the political climate. The interview was described as tense and awkward by multiple outlets. The endorsement could affect party unity and the upcoming midterm election in Michigan.

news.headline: Tucker Carlson claims Trump may order nuclear strike on Iran within days
news.summary: Former Fox News host Tucker Carlson posted on social media that President Donald Trump could launch a nuclear attack on Iran in the coming days. The claim references pressure from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and suggests a preemptive strike would be the "only military option." The statements have been widely circulated by both left- and right-leaning outlets, though no official U.S. government source has confirmed any such plan. The discussion raises concerns about the impact of speculative commentary on public perception of U.S. foreign policy.

news.headline: Trump says he would consider pardons for Elon Musk and aides if Democrats win Congress
news.summary: President Donald Trump told reporters he would be willing to offer protective pardons to Elon Musk and close aides if Democrats take control of the House and Senate after the midterm elections. He framed the move as a pre‑emptive safeguard against potential investigations. The statement comes as Democrats signal they may use new subpoena powers to examine the tech CEO and his companies. The proposal highlights the heightened partisan tension heading into the final two years of Trump's term.
